BROWSER_RENDERABILITY_RULES:
BROWSER PREVIEW REQUIREMENTS:

1. App.jsx MUST exist with: function App() { return (...); }
2. Functional components ONLY (no class components)
3. React hooks available globally: useState, useEffect, useRef, useMemo, useCallback, useReducer, useContext
4. Structure: App.jsx at root, components/ folder for UI, hooks/ folder for custom hooks

Will cause white screen:
- Missing App.jsx or App component
- Class components
- Circular dependencies
NO_INITIALIZATION_CODE:
DO NOT generate React initialization code - the system handles this automatically. FORBIDDEN: - ReactDOM.createRoot() - root.render() - document.getElementById("root") - import ReactDOM from "react-dom/client" CORRECT: Just export components - function App() { return
...
; } - export default App;
PACKAGE_MANAGEMENT_RULES:
BROWSER ENVIRONMENT - No npm packages available.

SUPPORTED:
- react, react-dom (import normally)
- framer-motion (global - NO import needed, use motion.div directly)
- Browser APIs: fetch(), localStorage, crypto.randomUUID(), Date

BANNED (use alternatives):
- axios → use fetch()
- lodash → use native JS
- uuid → use crypto.randomUUID()
- moment → use native Date
- prop-types → not needed
FRAMER_MOTION_USAGE:
motion and AnimatePresence are ALREADY DECLARED as globals. Use them directly in JSX:

<motion.div animate={{opacity:1}} />
<AnimatePresence>{show && <motion.div />}</AnimatePresence>

DO NOT declare them in any way:
- import { motion } from 'framer-motion'
- const { motion } = window
- const motion = anything
